newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures up sharply on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures up sharply on jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures were sharply higher, with S&P 500s rising the opening 7.00 point limit and then extending gains in volatile dealings.
S&Ps were locked up the opening limit the first 10 minutes of the session, and trade in the contract was then halted for two minutes according to exchange rules.
When trade resumed, the September S&P contract immediately jumped another 5.00 full points in choppy trade. Prices briefly moved in 1.00 point increments, compared with the normal 0.05 point ticks.
The S&P contract surpassed the old contract high by 13.00 points and reached a new all-time high of 929.00.

Strength in the bond market stemming from a jump in the U.S. unemployment rate to 5.0 percent contributed to gains in index futures as the data made it less likely the Federal Reserve would act soon to raise interest rates.
"The probability of a fed rate hike was about 20 percent yesterday," said Kurt Schultz, stock index analyst on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange for Refco Inc.
"The (employment) numbers confirmed a lack of a fed move."
The sharp jump also was positive for the technical outlook, and some expect further gains.
"I don't see why it couldn't go to 1000.00," sometime this year, said Jay Hohmann, head of stock index futures trading at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities of the S&P 500 index.
Hohmann said S&Ps consolidated for a brief period after rallies to about 850 and 900, so the next likely move to the 950 area is likely to be followed by another period of consolidation.
Floor traders said a few arbitrage buy programs were triggered early, when premiums widened on the rally.
However, the NYSE's index arbitrage rule went into effect quickly as the Dow Industrials rallied 50 points, which curtailed arb trading.
Traders pegged the S&P theoretical fair value premium at about 7.70 points, with buy programs likely above 8.50 points and sell programs probable at a premium under 6.90 points.

At 0936 CDT/1436 GMT, September S&P 500s were up 9.75 points at 925.25, Nasdaq 100s 9.75 higher at 999.00, Russell 2000s up 2.00 points to 401.50, KCBT Value Line futures up 6.00 points to 810.00, Nikkei 225 index futures off 90.0 to 20,270.0 and Midcap 400s up 1.65 points to 296.00.
